chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Husayn ibn Saif from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, how did the waiting period (iddah) of the divorced woman become three menstrual periods or three months, and how did the waiting period of the woman whose husband died become four months and ten days?'
He said, 'As for the waiting period of the divorced woman being three quru' (menstrual periods), it is for purifying the womb from pregnancy.'

As for the waiting period of the woman whose husband died, indeed Allah the Exalted stipulated a condition for women and stipulated a condition upon them, so He did not favor them in what He stipulated for them, nor did He diminish what He stipulated upon them.
As for what He stipulated for them in al-Ila' (oath of abstention from intercourse), it is four months, as He says: 'For those who swear abstention from their wives is the waiting of four months.'
For those who swear abstention from their wives is the waiting of four months.
So He did not allow anyone more than four months in al-Ila', due to His knowledge that it is the limit of the woman's patience regarding the man.
As for what He stipulated upon them, He commanded her to observe a waiting period if her husband dies: four months and ten days.
So He took from her for Himself at his death what He had taken for her from him during her life at the time of his al-Ila'.
Allah the Exalted says: 'So their waiting period is four months and ten days.'
So their waiting period is four months and ten days.
And He did not mention the ten days in the waiting period except together with the four months.
And He knew that the limit of the woman's patience in abstaining from intercourse is four months.
Therefore, from that, He made it obligatory upon her and for her.

key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: Waiting period of the woman whose husband died
key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: Waiting period of the divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind the waiting period for widows being four months and ten days?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the iddah of three menstrual periods for divorcees serves to ensure the womb is free from pregnancy (istibra'), while the four months and ten days for widows reflects the maximum limit of a woman's patience for abstaining from intercourse. He draws a parallel to the ruling of *ila'* (oath of abstention), noting that just as Allah set a four-month limit for husbands in *ila' as the peak of endurance, He established the widow's iddah to balance the rights and patience of both parties, ensuring justice in the transition of marital status.
